text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Tuesday.

LONDON - British stocks rose, though a sluggish start on Wall Street and market jitters ahead of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony before U.S. Congress Wednesday restrained the gains. The FTSE 100 index of leading shares added 13.6 points to 4,344.7.

FRANKFURT - Stocks surged, propelled by overnight Wall Street gains and a recovery in the dollar that sparked renewed interest in the German market. The 30-share DAX index jumped 49.0 points, or 1.54 percent, to 3,233.21 points.
PARIS - French shares also jumped, fuelled by Monday's gain on Wall Street and a solid dollar. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed rose 39.87 points or 1.55 percent to 2,607.72.
ZURICH - Swiss shares were driven higher by a rebound after Monday's losses and the firming U.S. dollar. The all-share SPI rose 24.52 points to 2,861.52.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks scored healthy gains as buying of blue chips picked up, stamping out early morning losses. Trade was subdued as Tuesday was the last trading day for February delivery. The Nikkei 225 rose 173.08 points or 0.92 percent to 19,070.07.

HONG KONG - A record-setting performance by HSBC led Hong Kong shares to a strong close as keen interest continued to drive China-related shares. The Hang Seng Index rose 144.57 points or 1.08 percent to 13,520.26.
SYDNEY - The Australian share market rallied as enthusiastic buyers came out of the woodwork. The All Ordinaries index added 18.2 points to 2,500.8.
JOHANNESBURG - South African stocks ended mixed. The all-share index gained 30.1 points to 7,203.2, the gold index added 9.2 points to 1,538.5, but the industrial index fell 15.1 points to 8,425.5.
